name: Gluetun AutoSwitch
description: Moves Gluetun to another VPN exit when a stream stays too slow, a provider keeps rejecting VOD or refuses it on this exit, a login is refused, a live source shows Cloudflare's block page, or a scheduled speed test falls below your minimums. Exits a provider refused are kept off for 30 days.
author: Brxdy22

fields.label: Auto switch
fields.help_text: Off = observe only: problems are logged as 'would switch'. On = really moves the VPN exit. A switch interrupts every stream on the tunnel for about 10 to 20 seconds.

fields.label: Allowed countries
fields.help_text: Countries to use. Only used when Allowed cities is empty: each switch then asks for a random server, moving to the next country if you pick several. At least one is required: Save is refused without one. An exit that breaks these rules, as after a Gluetun restart, is moved within about a minute, even with someone watching. After changing this, Save and refresh the page to update the city and server lists.

fields.label: Allowed cities
fields.help_text: Cities in your Allowed countries, tried in the order you pick them. These take priority over Allowed countries. Pick a country first: a city is only read while its country is allowed. Leave empty to use countries alone.

fields.label: Blocked countries
fields.help_text: Optional. Countries never to move to.

fields.label: Blocked cities
fields.help_text: Optional. Cities never to move to. With countries only, the plugin picks the city itself so a blocked one can't come up.

fields.label: Blocked exits
fields.help_text: Servers never to move to. Added automatically when a provider refuses VOD on an exit, and dropped after 30 days. Pick a server to block it yourself. Unselect one and Save to use it again. If an exit was added after you opened this page, refresh first: a Save from an older page can't remove anything.

fields.label: Blocked exits details
fields.help_text: Filled in automatically: address, server, city, which account blocked it, and when it expires. Refresh the page to see new entries. Edits here are replaced.

fields.label: Minimum speed (x real time)
fields.help_text: A stream counts as slow below this. 1.0 is exactly real time. It only moves the exit when no other stream of the same kind is keeping up, and once per stream every 30 minutes, because a stream still slow on a new exit is the feed's problem.

fields.label: Slow for (seconds)
fields.help_text: How long a stream must stay slow before anything happens.

fields.label: Minutes between switches
fields.help_text: Minimum wait after a switch.

fields.label: Maximum switches per hour
fields.help_text: Stops a provider problem, which no exit can fix, from cutting streams over and over.

fields.label: VOD rejections before switching
fields.help_text: How many VOD attempts one account may have refused on the current exit before moving. Needs the VOD Failover plugin, which logs each attempt.

fields.label: Count rejections within (minutes)
fields.help_text: Older rejections are forgotten. The count also restarts on a new exit.

fields.label: Rejection codes
fields.help_text: HTTP answers that mean the exit address was refused. 404 (title missing) and 458, 460 or 429 (connection limit) aren't offered: a new exit fixes none of those.

fields.label: Switch at the first blocked VOD
fields.help_text: When every server of an account answers 404 for a title, and a title that played before is refused too, the exit is refused, not the title. m3u-failover then holds the player while the exit moves and tries again, so playback starts a few seconds late instead of failing, and the exit goes on Blocked exits. Ignores Minutes between switches, but not the hourly limit. Needs Auto switch on and m3u-failover 1.2.

fields.label: Background VOD check every (minutes)
fields.help_text: Only while nobody is watching: m3u-failover asks each account for one byte of a title that played before. Nothing is logged while VOD works. If the exit is refused, it goes on Blocked exits and the exit moves before anyone presses play. Needs Auto switch on and m3u-failover 1.2. 0 turns it off.

fields.label: Login check every (minutes)
fields.help_text: Asks each Xtream account for its login page, which uses no stream connection, to notice a refused exit even when nobody is watching. 0 turns it off.

fields.label: Refused login checks before switching
fields.help_text: Checks in a row answering 520 to 527. This switch waits until nobody is watching.

fields.label: Gluetun URL
fields.help_text: Gluetun's control server as Dispatcharr sees it.

fields.label: Last speed test
fields.placeholder: No speed test has run yet.
fields.help_text: Filled in by each speed test. Refresh the page to see a new result. Edits here are replaced.

fields.label: Test every (minutes)
fields.help_text: Automatic speed test of the current exit, only when nobody is watching. About 340 MB each. 0 turns it off.

fields.label: Failed tests before switching
fields.help_text: Tests in a row below the minimums. A failed test is repeated after 5 minutes. The switch waits until nobody is watching.

fields.label: Minimum download (Mbps)
fields.help_text: On one connection, like a stream. Your heaviest stream so far used about 10 Mbps. 0 turns this check off.

fields.label: Minimum upload (Mbps)
fields.help_text: 0 turns this check off, which is recommended: streams only come down through the VPN.

fields.label: Maximum ping (ms)
fields.help_text: Ping to Cloudflare through the exit. 0 turns this check off.

fields.label: Provider ping limit (x usual)
fields.help_text: Fails when a provider's ping is this many times its usual, taken from recent healthy tests of the same server. Compared per provider, because some are simply far away. A rise seen from two different exits becomes the new usual. 0 turns this check off.

actions.label: Check status
actions.description: Shows the current exit, stream speeds and recent decisions.

actions.label: Change exit node
actions.description: Moves to the next allowed exit right away, even with Auto switch off. Interrupts every stream on the tunnel.

confirm.title: Change exit node?
confirm.message: This interrupts every stream on the tunnel for about 10 to 20 seconds.

actions.label: Run speed test
actions.description: Measures the current exit's download, upload and ping, plus ping to each provider. Takes about 20 seconds.

confirm.title: Run speed test?
confirm.message: This uses the VPN tunnel for about 20 seconds, which may briefly slow streams playing now.

actions.label: Ask the provider
actions.description: Asks every Xtream account now and shows each answer. Nothing is moved.

actions.label: Clear blocked exits
actions.description: Removes every exit from Blocked exits, so all of them can be used again.

confirm.title: Clear blocked exits?
confirm.message: Every blocked exit can be used again straight away.
